activation.title: Build your sermon step by step
activation.description: I will guide you through the 8 steps of study. You write each step in your own words; I provide data and questions, and confront when I detect a method error. I never write your answer.
activation.passageHint: Full passage (book + chapter + verse). The rest of the study builds on it.

cta.startGuidedDescription: Build your sermon step by step with a Socratic agent that guides and confronts.

error.activate: Could not activate the guide. Please try again.
error.runTurn: Could not process your reply. Please try again.

wordStudy.helperHint: Pick a word to see its original form and meaning. Then write YOUR discovery in the chat: what it contributes to the passage's message.
wordStudy.discoveryPrompt: This data is from the lexicon, not your answer. In your own words, write what this word contributes to THIS passage.

crossRef.helperHint: Pick a parallel and write YOUR note in the chat: why it relates to this passage.
crossRef.empty: No automatic parallels found. You can note one you know.
crossRef.discoveryPrompt: The parallel is from the cross-reference engine, not your answer. In your own words, write why it connects to THIS passage.

insight.helperHint: Fill the 5 parts in your own words. On submit they're saved exactly as you wrote them.
insight.centralIdeaPlaceholder: Your sermon's central claim, in one sentence.
insight.observationsHint: One per line; each with some substance.
insight.openQuestionPlaceholder: A question the text leaves for reflection.
insight.savedDoubtsHint: These questions came up during your study. Tap one to use it as your open question.
insight.anecdotePlaceholder: A pastoral illustration or anecdote (a couple of sentences).
insight.doxologicalPlaceholder: How this leads you to worship and respond to God (a couple of sentences).
insight.missing: Still needed to close the step:
insight.affirmation: Received. Your insight was saved exactly as you wrote it — it's your work, not the assistant's. That closes your study; continue in the editor to write the sermon.
